## This time: Quality Control and Filtration

- Number of unique genes in samples
- Cell counts per sample
- Ribosomal read counts
- Mitochondrial read counts
- Doublet cells


  

## Libraries and single-cell data

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- Load in the libraries (or install them) 

- Read in our data from day 1 with the readRDS function 

:::

::: {.column width=60%}

```{r}

# BiocManager::install(c("Seurat","SeuratWrappers", "scDblFinder") )

library(Seurat)
library(SeuratWrappers)
library(scDblFinder)

seu = readRDS("/varidata/researchtemp/hpctmp/single_cell_workshop_2026/day1/data/raw_seu.Rds")

```

:::

::::

## Number of cells

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- Cell quality and quantity are important.

- The first step is to make sure there are enough cells in each sample.

:::

::: {.column width=60%}

```{r}

barplot(table(seu@meta.data$orig.ident), ylab = "Number of cells") # Number of cells for each sample

```
:::
::::



## Number of cells
:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}


- Sample 6 looks pretty low compared to other cells. 
- *Ideally*, you want >2000 cells, but lower cell counts can still work.

:::

::: {.column width=60%}

```{r}

barplot(table(seu@meta.data$orig.ident), ylab = "Number of cells") # Number of cells for each sample

```
:::

::::

## Looking at the number of features

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- Feature count gives an idea of how many unique genes a sample's cells have transcribed. 

- This is **not** the number of reads.

- Samples 5 and 6 have a lot of features! They're different, but that might make sense for your experiment.

:::

::: {.column width=60%}

```{r Filtering Cells for Feature Count}

VlnPlot(seu, features = "nFeature_RNA") # Number of unique transcribed RNA features 

```

:::

::::

## Number of RNA reads in a cell

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

This *is* the number of reads in a cell. 

:::

::: {.column width=60%}
```{r}

VlnPlot(seu, features = "nCount_RNA") # Number of reads in each cell

```
:::

::::


## Finding cell ribosomal reads

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.columns width=40%}

- High ribosomal reads can indicate cell damage
- scRNA libraries often don't pick up rRNA

:::

::: {.columns width=60%}

```{r Filtering Cells for Ribosomal Read Content}

head(rownames(seu)[grepl("^Rp[sl]", rownames(seu))], n = 40)

seu <- PercentageFeatureSet(seu, pattern = "^Rp[sl]", col.name = "percent_ribo")

```
:::

::::


## Looking at ribosomal content of cells

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

VlnPlot(seu, features = "percent_ribo")

```
::::


## Combining read and feature count

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- Each dot is an individual cell, colored by sample

- "0.91" is the Pearson correlation relating RNA counts to features

:::

::: {.column width=60%}
```{r}

FeatureScatter(seu, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA",
               group.by = "sample")

```
:::

::::


## Mitochondrial reads

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- Mitochondrial genes' names start with "mt-"
- Cells with lots of mitochondrial genes are likely damaged and should be removed

:::

::: {.column width=60%}
 
```{r Finding Cells for Mitochondrial Reads}

rownames(seu)[grepl("^mt-", rownames(seu))]

seu <- PercentageFeatureSet(seu, pattern = "^mt-", col.name = "percent_mito")

```

:::

::::


## Combined look at mitochondrial reads

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

FeatureScatter(seu, feature1 = "nFeature_RNA", feature2 = "percent_mito", 
               group.by = "sample")

```

::::

## Filtering to keep quality cells

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40%}

- We'll use miQC, a tool packaged with Seurat 
- Uses `percent_mito` feature we built
- Also uses `nFeature_RNA`

:::

::: {.column width=60%}

```{r Filtering cells}

head(seu@meta.data, n = 3)

seu <- RunMiQC(seu,
          percent.mt = "percent_mito",
          nFeature_RNA = "nFeature_RNA",
          posterior.cutoff = 0.95,      # The probability a cell is part of a compromised distribution. Below the appointed cutoff will be marked to keep.
          model.slot = "flexmix_model" )

table(seu@meta.data$miQC.keep)

```
:::
::::

## See what changes with your data

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

seu <- subset(seu, subset = (miQC.keep == "keep"))

table(seu@meta.data$miQC.keep)

```


::::

## Doublets

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width="40%"}
- Unwanted pairs of cells that are analyzed as one 
- Don't cluster with other cells
- Might appear as an intermediate cell type
- Inflate the cell count
- Introduce noise
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](singlets_doublets.png){width=70% fig-align="center"}
:::

::::


## Filtering cells for doublets
:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

::: {.column width=40% }

- Doublets can be difficult to detect, but we have tools to find them. 

- We'll use one called `scDblFinder`, which doesn't work with Seurat objects. 

- It works with `SingleCellExperiment` objects. 

- Let's convert our Seurat object to a SCE object. 

:::

::: {.column width=60% fig-align="center"}
```{r}

seu = JoinLayers(seu)

seu = as.SingleCellExperiment(seu)

```
:::

::::

## Find the doublet filtration

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

seu = scDblFinder(seu)

```

::::


## Converting back to Seurat

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

seu <- as.Seurat(seu, counts = "counts", data = NULL)

table(seu@meta.data$scDblFinder.class)

```

::::


## Remove cells marked as doublets

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r}

seu <- subset(seu, subset = (scDblFinder.class == "singlet"))

table(seu@meta.data$scDblFinder.class)

```

::::

## Save your work!!

:::: {.columns style="align-items: center;"}

```{r, eval=FALSE}

saveRDS(seu, "/varidata/researchtemp/hpctmp/*your_folder*/scRNA_workshop_2026.rds")

```
